From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Simon Park <simon@arboretum.ai>
Date: 2027-06-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Preflight: capacity sketch request — Arboretum pilot

Hi Simon,

Thanks again for the call this morning — excited to move the pilot forward. To put together a lightweight capacity sketch (GPU SKU mix, rough cluster size, and burst tolerance) we usually start with a short traffic template so our pre-sales math matches your real workload. Can you attach a recent 24–72hr trace or fill the template I attached? Key things that matter for sizing:

- Average and peak concurrent sessions (or users)
- Peak burst rate (requests/sec) and typical burst duration
- Prompt token distribution (median / 90p / outliers) and response tokens
- Percent of requests that are streaming vs non-streaming
- Session stickiness / KV cache reuse expectations (how often a session reuses the same context)
- SLA targets (p95 latency, acceptable cold-start delay) and any fallback tolerances

If you prefer, a short CSV with one row per minute (timestamp, requests, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_response_tokens, streaming_pct) is perfect. I attached a sample_traffic_template.csv.

Goal: get a first-pass capacity sketch by Thursday so we can propose a dedicated pilot commitment and an initial cost estimate.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Sr Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Preflight: capacity sketch request — Arboretum pilot

Marissa —

Thanks, attaching a trimmed telemetry extract (arboretum_telemetry_week-21.csv). High level answers inline:

- Sustained concurrency (avg active sessions): ~120
- Typical steady-state RPS: ~40 requests/sec
- Peak bursts: up to ~2,400 concurrent sessions (~800 RPS equivalent) for 3–7 minutes (we see daily spikes after marketing pushes)
- Avg prompt tokens: 600 (median 420, 90p 1,150)
- Avg response tokens: 900 (median 720, 90p 1,600)
- Streaming: ~30% of requests use streaming; the rest are non-streamed generation
- Session stickiness: medium — about 60% of sessions reuse a KV cache across multiple turns over a 10–15 minute window
- P95 latency target for pilot: <= 350ms on generation-only paths; we can tolerate higher for long-form async jobs

Procurement copied for early notice; they may ask for an NDA and an initial SOW.

Let me know if you want fuller traces (we can scrub PII).

Simon Park
Head of Platform Engineering | Arboretum AI
simon@arboretum.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-02T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight: capacity sketch request — Arboretum pilot

Thanks Simon — this is great context and the sample looks usable. A few clarifying questions before I run a quick sketch:

1) Distribution shape: is the 90p prompt/response driven by a small fraction of very long sessions (authors writing drafts) or by many sessions that occasionally produce long outputs? That affects KV cache reuse and token accounting.
2) For streaming requests: do you expect partial token rendering for UI (i.e., client-side streaming) or are those server-side streaming transforms? Streaming changes GPU batching economics.
3) Any requirement for GPU isolation per tenant (e.g., data controls) or is multi-tenant on dedicated nodes acceptable?
4) Do you plan to use the same model for short vs long requests, or will you route long-form jobs to a different large-weight model?
5) Target pilot duration and expected RPS growth over 30 days (we assume +20% framing unless you tell us otherwise).

I'm going to produce two sketches: one assuming H100-heavy (best latency) and one with mixed A100/RTX options for cost parity. I'll drop an initial_capacity_sketch.xlsx in the thread when ready.

- Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Quick note from me: the burst profile (2,400 concurrent for ~5 minutes) is what pushes us from a tiny cluster to a medium reserved pool if Arboretum wants <500ms p95. Two thoughts to keep in mind:

- If Arboretum can accept slightly higher p95 during predictable daily bursts, we can reduce committed nodes and rely on short burst autoscale with a cost buffer.
- KV cache reuse (60%) is helpful — we should model hit-rate sensitivity at 50/60/70% in the sketch to show cost sensitivity.

Looping in Monica for session transience questions (monica handles cache TTL/cost impacts).
